Hi Sean —

Thanks for the call this morning. As part of our procurement and legal review, MedixPay needs a couple of concrete items to close the DPA:

1) A current roster of subprocessors (names, roles, country of operation, whether they handle encrypted token material).
2) A short attestation per subprocessor confirming whether any data is processed outside the EU and, if so, the legal basis or transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, or explicit carveout).
3) Confirmation of KMS key custody for EU customer keys (Do you hold KMS or is customer-managed?).

We'd like these as an excel + a signed PDF so our legal ops team can attach them to the DPA exhibit. Target for our internal review is next Tuesday.

Can you send the roster and a draft attestation (even a short paragraph per subprocessor) by EOD Friday UK time?

Thanks,
Tara

Senior Counsel, MedixPay

Marissa —

Received, thanks. A quick read-through from our side: good granularity on the roster. Two asks from legal ops: 

- The roster needs a column explicitly stating whether the subprocessors ever receive plaintext PII (not just tokenized identifiers). A simple Y/N is fine.
- For any subprocessors flagged as "non-EU processing", we need an explicit sentence saying whether the transfer is operationally avoidable (i.e., can you route EU customers to EU-only instances for those subprocessors or is cross-border processing required).

Also, we noticed one vendor (EdgeLogix) listed as operating in US/IE — can you confirm the primary control plane for that vendor and whether they have SCCs?

If you can add the plaintext-PII column and the routing note, we'll be in a much better place to attach these to the DPA exhibit. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Tara

(On a related note: is there an SLA or contractual language you typically use for KMS custody for EU customers? We'd like to reference it in procurement.)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor attestations + EU residency carveout

Tara / Rajiv —

Thanks — updates made. Summary of changes (see updated roster attached):

- Added "receives_plaintext_pii" column (Y/N) for each subprocessor. Our vendor intake confirms that only three subprocessors occasionally receive plaintext PII for troubleshooting: EdgeLogix (US), TransmitOps (US), and AuditFlow (IE). We flag them and attached evidence links.
- Added "eu_routing_possible" column with routing guidance. For EdgeLogix and TransmitOps we currently have geo-routing capability and can route EU customers to EU-only processing nodes for the majority of flows; however, EdgeLogix has an operational async batch job (US) for analytics that would still export hashed identifiers to the US unless we configure an EU-only analytics path (work required). We've noted the mitigations and timeline estimate (~3 weeks) in the notes cell.
- EdgeLogix SCCs: they have SCCs in place and we have their executed copy on file (link in tab 3).

KMS custody language: Our standard clause for customer-managed KMS (EU) is: "Customer retains sole administrative control and holding of KMS keys; Redwood does not export, store, or have administrative access to customer-managed keys." For platform-managed keys we provide a custody attestation referencing our key management procedures and HSM usage; we can include a short SLA addendum if you require it. Lauren, can you confirm if the SLA addendum language is appropriate to send to procurement?

Next steps: send final signed PDF attestation once you confirm the plaintext PII column and routing language are sufficient.

Thanks,
Marissa

Tara —

Appreciate the thorough asks. I reviewed Marissa's edits and proposed two small wording changes in the attestation PDF (clarity on "occasional plaintext" and an explicit note that routing controls are a configuration option and not a guaranteed product-level isolation unless contracted).

Proposed SLA addendum language (short version):
- "For customers who elect customer-managed KMS, Redwood will not access or export customer keys and will provide an attestation of key custody on request. For Redwood-managed keys, Redwood will maintain hardware-backed key storage and provide documented key rotation and access-control procedures. Any custodian SLA for key recovery or emergency access must be negotiated as a separate addendum."

If this is acceptable, we'll generate a signed attestation PDF and the final roster for you to attach. Otherwise flag any redlines and we can iterate quickly.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts & Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
